ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A mass spectrometer is an important tool for determining the mass of charged particles and analyzing isotopes, and its structural principle is shown in the figure. The particle source S emits two kinds of positively charged isotope particles A and B. When the two kinds of particles come out from S, their velocities are very small and can be ignored. After being accelerated by the accelerating electric field, the particles enter perpendicularly into a bounded uniform magnetic field (shown by the wireframe in the figure), and finally hit the photographic plate. It is measured that the ratio of the distances from the points where particles A and B hit the photographic plate to the entrance is 5:4, so what is the ratio of the times they move in the magnetic field?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the upper part of the figure is a rectangular bounded region, inside which multiple "×" symbols indicate that the direction of the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward; near the right side of the lower boundary of the rectangle there is a particle entrance, connected to the slit S1 below. At the lower right is marked particle source S, and particles enter the magnetic field from S after passing through the accelerating electric field and slit S1. On the left side of the lower boundary of the rectangle is marked "photographic plate," and the particles hit the plate after being deflected in the magnetic field; the horizontal distance from the entrance to the hit point corresponds to the diameter of the semicircular trajectory of the particle in the magnetic field. Then reason: A and B are isotope positive ions, with the same charge q; they start from rest and are accelerated by the same accelerating voltage U, so qU=1/2 mv^2. After entering the same uniform magnetic field, they undergo circular motion, with radius r=mv/(qB). Eliminating v from the two equations gives r=sqrt(2mU/q)/B, so under the conditions that q, U, and B are the same, r∝sqrt(m). The problem gives that the ratio of the distances from the hit points to the entrance is 5:4, and this distance d=2r, so r_A:r_B=5:4. Therefore m_A:m_B=(r_A:r_B)^2=25:16. What the particles move through in the magnetic field is a semicircle, and the time is half of the cyclotron period t=πm/(qB). Since q and B are the same, t∝m, so t_A:t_B=25:16.
